item.title: Penn State Hires Matt Campbell as Next Head Coach
item.description: Updated 10:11 p.m. Dec. 5. The Nittany Lions finally have their guy. After a nearly two-month search, Penn State has reached an agreement with Matt Campbell to be the football program's next head coach, pending approval on Monday by the Board of Trustees, Athletic Director Pat Kraft confirmed in a statement Friday night after multiple reports indicated a deal had been finalized. item.title: Centre County Cleaning Service Owner Accused of Stealing Nearly $67K From Former Client
item.description: The owner of a Centre County cleaning company was arrested Friday after police said she stole thousands of dollars from a former customer. Megyn A. Frank, the owner of Happy Valley Elite Cleaning, is accused of using debit and credit card information she had on file to take more $66,780 from a Huston Township man. item.description: With Penn State’s hiring of head coach Matt Campbell now official, one of his first responsibilities will be assembling a coaching staff and roster heading into 2026. The final product will likely be a Frankenstein group of returning Nittany Lions, Cyclones and new transfers and recruits. The good news for Campbell is the transfer portal era has sped up the timeline for rebuilds, allowing a one-year turnaround if executed properly. item.title: Penn State to Retain Terry Smith After Hiring Matt Campbell
item.description: Updated 10 p.m. Dec. 5. Terry Smith isn't going anywhere. Penn State's interim head coach will remain on staff under newly hired head coach Matt Campbell, Athletic Director Pat Kraft confirmed in a statement on Friday night. ESPN's Pete Thamel reported he's agreed to a four-year deal, half the duration of Campbell's eight-year contract. item.title: Penn State Wrestling Defeats Drexel 43-3
item.description: No. 1 Penn State wrestling (2-0, 0-0 Big Ten) secured its second dual win of the season with a 43-3 demolition of the Drexel Dragons (2-1, 1-0 EIWA) Friday night at the Daskalakis Athletic Center in Philadelphia. item.title: Reports: Penn State to Play in Pinstripe Bowl
item.description: Penn State's postseason destination has been revealed. According to multiple reports, the Nittany Lions will play in the Bad Boy Mowers Pinstripe Bowl, which will take place on Dec. 27 at Yankee Stadium. Their opponent will be an ACC team, meaning Virginia, SMU, Miami, Pitt, Georgia Tech, Duke, Cal, Clemson, NC State, Louisville and Wake Forest are options, having all clinched bowl eligibility.
